output.headline: Investigation into Channel dinghy incident leads to Daniel Thomas’s arrest
output.standfirst: Daniel Thomas, 37, is being held on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life after footage appeared to show him slashing a dinghy in the Channel with a rescue worker onboard
output.bodyHtml:
Police have arrested the far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas on suspicion of “criminal damage with intent to endanger life”, after he filmed himself appearing to slash the side of a dinghy in the middle of the Channel while a rescuer was onboard.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said a 37-year-old man, of no fixed abode, had been arrested after a boat carrying an emergency responder was damaged in the Channel. The man was arrested “on suspicion of destroying ships or fixed platforms or endangering their safety”.

Police said he remained in custody on Thursday, also suspected of committing “criminal damage, criminal damage with intent to endanger life, and conduct endangering ships, structures or individuals”.

The force said it had been examining footage livestreamed by Thomas, which reportedly appears to show him using a knife to stab and slash an inflatable dinghy in the middle of the Channel after asylum seekers had been helped to safety, but with a French rescue worker who had just got onboard.

Thomas’s footage appeared to show him approaching one of the dinghies, which was empty, shouting: “Let’s get rid of that boat.” After the rescue worker got onboard, Thomas shouted: “Get off the boat. You’ve got time to get off the boat.” The footage then shows Thomas’s boat speeding away before the rescue worker climbed back on the larger boat.

More than 200,000 people watched the livestreamed footage, in which Thomas, who goes by the name Danny Tommo, filmed himself from a boat as he spent the afternoon tracking two dinghies carrying asylum seekers from France to the UK.

Thomas, a longtime associate of fellow far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, AKA Tommy Robinson, had repeatedly told his followers they should march silently, without violence, and avoid doing anything that could lead to arrests. This summer he gathered dozens of nationalist protest groups under the umbrella anti-immigration movement Patriot Platform, which was behind marches this month in Dover and Portsmouth, when masked men in black gathered and protested over immigration and asylum policy.

A police officer is seen, in a 56-second clip uploaded to Thomas’s YouTube platform on Wednesday night, telling him he was being arrested on suspicion of criminal damage “recklessly endangering someone’s life” — footage Thomas apparently managed to film and upload before police were able to stop him.

Thomas said: “I understand. I knew this was coming.”

Most small boats carrying asylum seekers across to the UK are escorted to shore by rescue services or Border Force vessels, and no unescorted small boats had been recorded since 6 September 2025 — until two uncontrolled landings from the Channel in two days brought renewed focus on the Home Office’s handling of small-boat arrivals, amid which Thomas’s arrest came.

A total of 21 people were detained after a boat evaded Border Force to reach the beach of Samphire Hoe in Dover on Wednesday, a second uncontrolled landing after another dinghy reached Folkestone on Monday morning, prompting the education secretary, Lucy Powell, to say: “You can’t stop everything all of the time”.

Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, has responded by ordering an urgent review by Border Security Command, after describing the failure to intercept the two boats as “not acceptable”.

Powell, speaking on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme, said: “Of course, it’s a concern. That’s why the home secretary has demanded and ordered this urgent review, because this is not what we want to see. This is not acceptable.”
